decision: Retain the qualified offline durable authorization and guarded-store candidate. Integrate all original full schedulers and actual process-failure recovery next; current collectors, financial backend and deployment remain unchanged.
falsifier: An unavailable inserted/refreshed observation, original normalization mismatch, missing raw/authorization bypass, erased original obligation, source/identity corruption accepted on reopen, or disagreement in archived reproduction updates or falsifies the corresponding claim.
hypothesis: Durable service availability enforcement must preserve each actual frozen producer runtime and remain effective when its store recovers orphan raw files.
limitations: Storage-boundary qualification only; full original service-backed scheduler, CLI and migration acceptance remain outstanding.
Synthetic candle transport and deliberate delay between the inner session return report and outer original caller receipt; no economic or production latency claim.
Actual close/reopen and SQL failure are tested; real OS kill/restart, power loss and complete admission/return/binding crash phases remain unqualified.
Recovery requires already issued exact service authorization; a saved return alone is not automatically authorized.
Native availability telemetry, whole-study startup performance, memory cost and full-grid accounting remain integration requirements.

Trusted local hashes do not defend against a compromised host. Coverage is 516/536 statements and 124/144 branches over seven affected modules, not whole-system or complete original-producer coverage.
Fifty-eight historical integration fixture tests were skipped in the broad suite because their separate selectors were not supplied.
